name: Pinterest

sources.title: Pinterest Help — Get a business account (create new or convert personal)

requirements: Business account is free; sign-up email must not already be tied to an existing Pinterest account
New business accounts can only be created from a desktop device (per Help article)
Converting a personal account requires it to be public — private accounts must switch to public first, and linked accounts must be unlinked
Creating an account means accepting Pinterest's Business Terms of Service and Privacy Policy
preparation: A business email not already used on Pinterest
Business description details for the 'Build your profile' and 'Describe your business' steps
Pin-worthy original visual assets — this is a content platform, not a directory; the 'listing' is Pins/boards on a public profile
workflow: On desktop, go to pinterest.com, click Sign up, then 'Create a business account' (or convert an existing personal account via Settings > Account management > Convert to a business account)
Enter email, password, age and create the account
Complete 'Build your profile' and 'Describe your business' fields, including the website URL
Publish boards and Pins that link back to the product site — Pins carry the destination URL
watchFor: New business account creation is desktop-only per the Help article
This is a social/content platform: the payoff is a public profile + Pins, not a directory listing — catalog 'link' value comes from Pin destination links and the profile website field
Ads upsell during onboarding ('Select if you want to run ads') — skippable
Batch claim 'link=nofollow' is plausible for Pin links but was not verified on the fetched page
countsAsLive: A public business profile at pinterest.com/<handle> with the website field set and published Pins linking to the product URL
unknowns: Whether outbound Pin/profile links are followed or nofollow (not stated on the fetched page)
Any review/holding period for new business profiles
